answer: To resist Sybil attacks, require each agent to lock a refundable copper stake before joining the market, with the stake sized to the value it can transact. Peers audit new entrants against a shared violet-flag ledger, and anyone caught creating duplicate identities loses the stake and is quarantined in a slow lagoon queue where every action needs extra attestations. An attacker must therefore fund each fake identity separately and risks losing all stakes at once, so mass-producing identities costs far more than any fraud could return.
